title: [BUG] fcvt.s.d misses UF on boundary cases that round to the minimum normal single
body:
CVA6 reports incorrect fflags for a boundary fcvt.s.d case. The converted single-precision result matches Spike, but the underflow flag is missing.

I reproduced this on current master (02e11e3b9d9e6a087dc4811b933bf0cc80156e1a) with cv64a6_imafdc_sv39, using spike vs veri-testharness.

The minimal case is:

- input: 0x380fffffe0000000
- instruction: fcvt.s.d
- rounding mode: RNE

Both Spike and CVA6 produce the same final single-precision result:

But fflags differ:
- Spike: 0x03 (NX|UF)
- CVA6 RTL: 0x01 (NX)

Observed mismatch:
```
Mismatch[1]:
spike[1427] : pc[0000000080003020] csrrs   t2, fflags, zero: t2:0000000000000003
veri-testharness[1427] : pc[0000000080003020] csrrs   t2, fflags, zero: t2:0000000000000001
```

So this is not a wrong-result bug. The result value itself matches. The issue is that UF is not reported.

We suspect the RTL design file causing the error is fpnew_cast_multi.sv, where uf_after_round only checks whether the rounded exponent field is 0, missing the carry from denormal to min normal.

Minimal reproducer:
```
  .section .text
  .globl main
  main:
    li   t0, 0
    csrw frm, t0

    li   t0, 0x380fffffe0000000
    fmv.d.x ft0, t0

    csrw fflags, x0
    fcvt.s.d ft1, ft0
    fmv.x.w  t1, ft1
    csrr     t2, fflags

    li   a0, 0
    jal  exit
```

fix_commits.messageHeadline: fpnew_cast_multi: Fix underflow detection logic at subnormal-nomal

Exactly the same UF flag missing bug in Xuantie C910 https://github.com/revyos/revyos/issues/47.

0077d9e buggy code before fix  commit cb3f0e5:

|                                    | Value                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **CEX input**                      | `0x380FFFFFD0000002` (RUP)                             |
| **FP64 true exponent**             | −127 = FP32 emin − 1 ✓                                 |
| **FP32 pre-round 23-bit fraction** | `0x7FFFFF` = all 23 bits 1 ✓                           |
| **Rounding action**                | `0x7FFFFF + 1 = 0x800000` → carry out → exponent 0 → 1 |
| **RTL result**                     | `0x00800000` (numerically correct)                     |
| **RTL fflags**                     | `0x01` (NX only — **UF missing**)                      |
| **Spec fflags**                    | `0x03` (NX\|UF — correct)                              |

### Exact the same cornel scene

1. **Condition 1** — exp of original result = emin−1 = −127 (FP32) ✓  
2. **Condition 2** — first N=23 explicit fraction bits all 1s (`0x7FFFFF`) ✓

title: [F2I BUG] FP64 to UINT32 cast incorrectly raises NX instead of NV for large negative inputs that wrap to zero after rounding
body:
## Bug description
Inputs to reproduce the bug which concerns the `fpnew_cast_multi` unit

```
operands_i  = 0xc1effffffffbffff  // FP64 negative value
op_i        = F2I
op_mod_i    = 1                   // unsigned cast
src_fmt_i   = FP64
int_fmt_i   = INT32
rnd_mode_i  = RNE
```

Expected Output (computed by reference model [cvfpu-uvm](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu-uvm))
```
result_o = 0x00000000
status_o.NV = 1    // invalid operation: negative float cast to unsigned
status_o.NX = 0
```
Actual Output
```
result_o = 0x00000000
status_o.NV = 0    // missing
status_o.NX = 1    // incorrectly raised
```
## Root cause
The first check is done at this stage
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/a74d99a32bd11ce0b05a82b0d6d26f98df3bba65/src/fpnew_cast_multi.sv#L445-L450
The input unbiased exponent of `31` is just below the `of_before_round` threshold for uint32 `(INT_WIDTH - 1 + op_mod = 32)`, so no pre-rounding overflow is detected and the value proceeds through the normal cast path.

With `denorm_shamt = MAX_INT_WIDTH - 1 - input_exp_q = 0`, the integer part fills all 32 bits:
```
final_int            = 0xFFFFFFFF
round_sticky_bits    = 2'b11       // R=1, S=1
```
With `RNE`  rounding mode and `RS = 2'b11 `(strictly greater than 1/2 ulp), `fpnew_rounding` unit sets `round_up = 1`.

This causes the absolute rounded value to wrap (overflow):
`abs_rounded_o = 0xFFFFFFFF + 1 = 0x100000000 → truncated to 0x00000000`

https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/a74d99a32bd11ce0b05a82b0d6d26f98df3bba65/src/fpnew_cast_multi.sv#L623

`rounded_int_res_zero` is wrongly set to 1.

This corrupts the only remaining guard for the negative-to-unsigned special case:
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/a74d99a32bd11ce0b05a82b0d6d26f98df3bba65/src/fpnew_cast_multi.sv#L729-L732

```
assign int_result_is_special = ...
    (input_sign_q & op_mod_q2 & ~rounded_int_res_zero);
//   1            & 1         & ~1                      = 0  ← not triggered
```

With `of_before_round = 0`, `of_after_round` skipped (negative sign guard), and `int_result_is_special = 0`, the result takes the normal path, producing the correct value `0x00000000` by coincidence but raising **NX** instead of **NV**.

title: [BUG] DIV request lost following flush causing hang in simulation
body: ## Observed behavior The test executed is `fpu_op_group_test.svh` and `seed=1760627103` (`OP_GROUP=DIVSQRT`, `fmt inside {FP32, FP64, FP16}`) in [cvfpu-uvm](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu-uvm). During this test, random division and square-root requests are issued, with a flush-on-the-fly randomly asserted during execution. The following sequence is observed as shown in the waveform: 1. Request A is accepted by the DUT. 2. A flush is asserted on the next clock cycle while request A is still in-flight. 3. Request B is sent after the flush. 3. The testbench waits indefinitely for a response for request B and the simulation hangs. ## Root cause The affected unit is `fpnew_divsqrt_th_64_multi.sv`, the wrapper around the C910 T-Head div/sqrt unit. Specifically, the `func_sel` and `op_sel` registers, which are two pulses that trigger the launch of the div/sqrt execution, are not cleared on flush: https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/3eb6afeab2cb33f7d8689222955d0171aeb3a801/src/fpnew_divsqrt_th_64_multi.sv#L336-L342 Since these pulses are not cleared by flush, a flush occurring between request acceptance and the actual launch of execution leaves the unit in an inconsistent state, causing subsequent requests to hang.
